open_points.subject: resolved not_applied operation-element conclusion
open_points.text: “`not_applied`: the element waits again with reason `owner_approval`” conflicts with “the element is not reached any more, so the advance reaches it again” and “whose attempt the owner resolved `not_applied`, is not reached and so is ready”
open_points.question: After `resolve_unknown_outcome` records `not_applied` but before a fresh approval exists, what conclusion must `effects.operation_element_conclusion` return so that `run_graph.plan_run` knows whether the element is waiting or ready to be reached?
options: Return `not reached`/ready until `effects.reach_operation_element` requests the fresh approval
Return `waiting(owner_approval)` but separately mark this wait actionable by advance
Keep it waiting and have `continue_after_resolution` call `reach_operation_element` directly
open_points.default_guess: Return `not reached`/ready, let the ordinary advance reach it once, and then return `waiting(owner_approval)` after the fresh approval request exists.

open_points.subject: recovery after a fresh approval was already requested
open_points.text: “an element whose approval was decided, or whose attempt the owner resolved `not_applied`, is not reached and so is ready” does not say how a later, still-`requested` fresh approval affects that rule
open_points.question: If `not_applied` was resolved and a fresh approval request was committed, but the following run-progress write was lost before restart, does recovery preserve the existing `owner_approval` wait or treat the element as ready and reach it again?
options: The existing requested fresh approval makes the wait hold, so recovery preserves it
The resolved `not_applied` always makes the element ready; reaching it discovers the existing request and waits again
open_points.default_guess: Preserve the existing requested fresh approval as a holding `owner_approval` wait.

open_points.subject: meaning of a decided approval during recovery
open_points.text: “an element whose approval was decided ... is not reached and so is ready” includes both `approved` and `refused`, while a refusal writes `refused_by_owner` and must end the run `refused` before any element is reached
open_points.question: Does “approval was decided” mean only an approval decided `approved`, or how must recovery distinguish `approved` from `refused` here?
options: Only `approved` makes an otherwise unconcluded element ready
Both decisions are examined, with `refused` taking precedence and ending the run
Every decided approval makes the element ready
open_points.default_guess: Interpret the phrase as `approved` only; a `refused_by_owner` conclusion takes precedence and ends the run.

open_points.subject: sandbox_runner.read_runner_report malformed report result
open_points.text: “An unreadable or partial report is not decoded into outputs” while the operation lists no error and no output variant for an unreadable, partial, or over-bound report
open_points.question: What exact result does `read_runner_report` return when framing is invalid, the report is partial, or the channel bound is exceeded, so that `sandbox` can apply the A03 outcome order?
options: A distinct `invalid_report` result that `sandbox` classifies as `crashed`
A synthetic escaped-exception report classified as `crashed`
An empty report whose process exit determines the outcome
open_points.default_guess: Return a distinct `invalid_report` result, which `sandbox` classifies as `crashed` unless an earlier timeout or resource limit wins.

open_points.subject: assemble_mapped_lists with several oversized outputs
open_points.text: “Every delivered list of the node is measured before any of them is written or delivered ... or that one list exceeds `stored_value_bytes_max`”
open_points.question: When more than one delivered output list exceeds the ceiling, what must `assemble_mapped_lists` return, and in what output-port order is the reported list selected?
options: Return all oversized output ports in output-port name order
Return only the first oversized port in output-port name order
Return only a node-level over-ceiling result without identifying a port
open_points.default_guess: Return only the first oversized output port in Unicode code-point order, while still measuring all delivered lists before returning.

open_points.subject: run_graph representation of mapped-list ceiling failure
open_points.text: “a mapped list over `stored_value_bytes_max` failing its node with no record” and “The conclusion of every element” do not define a returned node-level conclusion for a mapped node whose elements all succeeded but whose assembled list is oversized
open_points.question: How does `plan_run` represent this recordless aggregate-node failure—including its status/detail—so dependants become `upstream_failed`, the run becomes `failed`, and readers derive the same explanation?
options: A node-level `contract_violation` with detail `value_too_large`, separate from element conclusions
A generic node-level failed conclusion with no status or detail
Only downstream `upstream_failed` drafts plus a failed run status
A synthetic element conclusion despite the rule that no record represents the failure
open_points.default_guess: Return a separate node-level `contract_violation` conclusion with detail `value_too_large`, without creating a NodeExecution.
